Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Round 3 1. Lookout Phase 4 2. Production Phase 5 3. Action Phase 5.1 Construct a location 5.2 Develop a location 5.3 Make a deal 5.4 Raze location from your hand 5.5 Raze opponent's location 5.6 Use an action from a location 5.7 Use an action from your faction board 5.8 Use another player's open production location 5.9 Take a connection card 5.10 Play a connection card 5.11 Place a shield token on a location (free action) 5.12 Pass 6 4. Check for Game End 7 5. Cleanup Phase 8 End Game Scoring Overview Play cards to your area in order to earn points. When a player has 25 victory points (VPs), the current round finishes and then whoever has the most VPs (including end game scoring) wins! Round The round is split into five phases, each of which is completed by every player before moving to the next, the phases are: 1. Lookout phase 2. Production phase 3. Action phase 4. Check for game end 5. Cleanup phase 1. Lookout Phase First, reveal n+1 cards, where n is the number of players (e.g. 4 cards in a 3-player game). Then: • Players take turns taking a new card in clockwise order. • After each player has taken 1 card, discard remaining cards. Then draw n+1 cards again, and: • Starting with the last player and proceeding counter-clockwise, each player takes a card. • After each player has taken 1 card again, discard the remaining cards. 2. Production Phase First, gain resources according to your faction board. Usually this includes 3 workers 3 , 1 resource ⚙️/💳/🔫/⛽, 1 connection token > , and 1 card 🟔 . Second, each deal provides the good depicted on the card. Third, each production location produces goods (including open production cards). 3. Action Phase In clockwise order, each player takes a single action or passes until all players pass. If you pass then: • you cannot take additional actions • your locations cannot be razed or interacted with in any other way, e.g., use open production locations. The actions are: Construct a location Build a location by spending the number of grey connection tokens > equal to the card's Distance value. Earn any building bonuses and if building a production location (including open production locations), take the goods from the supply. Develop a location Build a location on top of an existing location by spending a brick and removing the old location. You earn 1 VP after developing. The new location must have at least 1 matching symbol with the old location. Ruins (and cards without icons like Radioactive Colony) can be built over with any type. Earn any building bonuses and if building a production location (including open production locations), take the goods from the supply. Any resources or tokens that were on the old card (if they were in "storage") are kept. Make a deal Spend the number of blue connection tokens > equal to the card's Distance value, and then turn the card upside down to show its Deal value. Immediately take the depicted good. Raze location from your hand Discard a card and spend the number of red connection tokens > equal to the card's Distance value. Take the goods shown in the spoils field. Raze opponent's location Spend the number of red connection tokens > equal to the location's Defense value (3 for Production, 4 for Feature, 5 for Action). Take the goods shown in the spoils field. The location's owner takes the good in the Deal field and turns the location upside down to indicate that the location is now a Ruin. Use an action from a location Spend the goods to perform the card action and keep the goods on the card to remember you used it this round, as each action can only be used once per round. Use an action from your faction board Spend the goods to perform the faction action and keep the goods on the faction board to remember you used it this round, as each action can only be used once per round. Use another player's open production location Spend a worker to earn the good on the opponent's open production location. The opponent takes a worker from the supply. You cannot send a worker to your own open production location. Each open production location can only be used once per round. Take a connection card Spend 2 workers to take a face-up connection card. Play a connection card Play a connection card and earn the goods on it. Place a shield token on a location (free action) Place a shield token on a location to increase its defense value by 1. Each location can only have 1 shield token. Pass Pass for the round and do not take any more actions. 4. Check for Game End If one player has 25 VPs or more, do not go to the Cleanup Phase, and instead calculate the final score for each player. 5. Cleanup Phase • You can use the storage ability on any locations to save goods. All other goods (resources, workers, contact tokens, shields) in your personal supply and on your cards are returned to the general supply. • Beside stored goods, you can only keep cards in between rounds. • Discard all face-up connection cards. • Pass the first player token to the left and start a new round. End Game Scoring Each player adds 1 VP per location (but 0 VP per Ruin) to their current score. In the case of a tie, use the following tie breakers in order: • The player with the most total goods • The player with the most locations • If still tied, share the victory

[Rating: 1/10] Rulebook was an infernal piece of crap. The sheer magnitude of its bullshit is mindboggling.  Don't know what seizures the designer experienced to write such an annoying, disgusting and confusing rulebook. As if he is mocking the player for purchasing such garbage and has no regard for his own game. Deplorable. Ridiculous. Wildly annoying.  The game itself was below average. But the rulebook ruined everything. I will never play it again. I'm glad that I didn't spend a dollar for it.

[Rating: 1/10] Solid tableau builder with nice player interaction. Unfortunately it needs to keep swapping expansions in and out to keep the experience from getting stale and it takes a little too long with anything more than 2 players.

[Rating: 2/10] Very bad and bland tableau/settlement builder?  I remember the similar but yet different tokens were confusing all of us.   Just slightly above the worst games i ever played. But just barely.

[Rating: 3/10] Mean and aggressive in the worst, kick-your-sandcastle kind of way. The core gameplay with the cards and tableau building is good but I prefer attacking in games built around that conceit and not when it's thrown into an engine building contest.

[Rating: 3/10] This felt very clunky to me. I prefer Imperial Settlers to this one but not by much. This suffer from the same problem. The game takes longer and longer the more it goes on. Boring!
